skill.name: scientific-schematics
skill.description: Create scientific diagrams from natural-language prompts using OpenRouter image generation and an AI quality review loop. The skill targets publication-style schematics, flowcharts, architectures, pathways, and technical figures.
skill.summary: Generate publication-style scientific schematics with AI review and iterative refinement.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: I confirmed intended OpenRouter API calls, local image and log writes, broad .env loading, and API key propagation on a child command line. Most static hits in Markdown, examples, tests, and base64 image handling are false positives. No prompt injection or hidden malicious intent was found in reviewed files.

remediation.issue: API key is passed to a child process as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the key through the child process environment or call the generator directly instead of adding --api-key to argv.

remediation.issue: The AI script searches parent directories for .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicit .env path or require OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the current environment.

remediation.issue: Generated images and review logs are written to user-selected paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate output paths, avoid overwriting existing files by default, or constrain writes to a figures directory.

remediation.issue: Prompts and images are sent to OpenRouter for generation and review.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external data flow clearly and advise users not to include sensitive unpublished data.

content.value_statement: Researchers need clear scientific figures without rebuilding diagrams manually. This skill generates publication-style schematics and reviews them against document-specific quality targets.
actual_capabilities: Generates scientific diagrams from natural-language prompts.
Uses OpenRouter image generation for schematic output.
Reviews generated images with a Gemini quality-check loop.
Saves versioned image files and a review log.
Supports document-type quality thresholds for journals, posters, talks, and reports.
Provides both command-line and Python API usage paths.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key and network access.
Generated scientific content still needs expert review before publication.
Writes image and review-log files to the selected output location.
Image quality depends on prompt specificity and model behavior.

use_cases.title: Create manuscript figures
use_cases.description: Generate CONSORT flows, pathways, and mechanism diagrams for early manuscript drafts.

use_cases.title: Prepare thesis visuals
use_cases.description: Turn method descriptions into clear figures for chapters, defenses, and posters.

use_cases.title: Draft technical diagrams
use_cases.description: Create architecture and workflow schematics with review notes for documentation teams.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single figure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scientific-schematics to generate a simple diagram of [topic]. Include the main components, labels, and flow direction.

prompt_templates.title: Add publication constraints
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the figure targets a specific document type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [journal/poster/presentation] schematic for [topic]. Use clear labels, high contrast, and a left-to-right layout.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a complex system
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for multi-step processes or architectures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a schematic showing [system]. Include each module, data flow, key annotations, and accessibility-friendly colors.

prompt_templates.title: Produce review-ready output
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a publication-ready figure for [study]. Apply the journal threshold, save versioned outputs, and summarize quality issues.

output_examples.input: A researcher requests a CONSORT participant flow diagram for a randomized trial.
output: Versioned PNG files show screening, exclusion, randomization, follow-up, and analysis groups.
A review log records the quality score and improvement notes.

output_examples.input: A student asks for a transformer architecture diagram for a presentation.
output: The generated figure shows encoder and decoder blocks with attention connections.
The review step checks readability, label quality, and layout clarity.

output_examples.input: A documentation writer needs a system workflow schematic for a technical report.
output: The output image presents modules, arrows, and labeled data movement.
The final copy is saved at the requested output path.

best_practices: Give precise component names, counts, and flow direction in the prompt.
Choose the document type that matches the final use of the figure.
Review generated images for scientific accuracy before sharing or publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague prompts such as make a diagram.
Do not treat generated labels or relationships as automatically correct.
Do not store long-lived API keys in shared shell profiles or repositories.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an OpenRouter API key for image generation and review.

faq.question: Can it create journal-ready figures?
faq.answer: It can create publication-style drafts, but a domain expert should verify every figure.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It saves versioned image files, a final image copy, and a review log.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. The generation and review steps call external AI models through OpenRouter.

faq.question: Can I use it from Python?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository includes a Python generator class and command-line wrapper.

faq.question: What diagrams are best suited?
faq.answer: It works best for flowcharts, architectures, pathways, circuits, and scientific process diagrams.
